questions.q: What is the key difference between an environment variable's definition and its current value?
options: There is no difference — they are the same thing
The definition (name, data type, default) travels inside the managed solution; the current value is set separately per environment
The current value travels inside the solution; the definition is set per environment
Definitions only exist in Production, values only exist in Dev
questions.explain: The definition is the shared shape every environment agrees on and moves with the solution. The current value is unmanaged and set independently in each environment, which is what lets the same flow use different values per environment.

questions.q: What does a connection reference store, that an environment variable does not?
options: A server name or URL
A JSON configuration blob
Which saved connection (login or service account) a connector action should use
The flow's trigger condition
questions.explain: A connection reference abstracts which specific saved connection a connector action uses, so each environment can map it to a different account without editing the flow. Environment variables store data values, not credentials.

questions.q: Castlebridge's flow has 'sql-castlebridge-dev.database.windows.net' typed directly into the SQL Server action. What happens when this flow is moved to Production?
options: Power Automate automatically rewrites it to the production server name
It keeps pointing at the dev server, because the value was never externalized
The flow fails to import at all
It prompts the maker to choose a new server during import
questions.explain: A hardcoded value has no mechanism to change per environment. Only values stored in an environment variable (or connection reference, for credentials) get prompted for and remapped on import.

questions.q: When does Power Apps ask you to supply values for a solution's environment variables?
options: Only when you manually open the Environment Variables list
During solution import into a target environment
Never — values must be set by editing the flow directly
Only for environment variables of type Secret
questions.explain: The solution import screen lists each environment variable that needs a value for the target environment, with a field to supply or override it right there during import.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a valid environment variable data type?
options: Text
Secret
Data source
Flow trigger
questions.explain: Environment variables support Text, Number, Two options, JSON, Secret, and Data source. 'Flow trigger' is not a data type — triggers are a property of the flow itself, not something an environment variable holds.
